rules.description: The resale exemption applies to tangible personal property purchased for the purpose of resale in the ordinary course of the buyer's business.
eligible_product_categories: all tangible personal property intended for resale
rules.summary: Tangible personal property purchased solely for resale qualifies; buyer must be a registered retailer or wholesaler.

rules.description: The buyer claiming a resale exemption must be registered with the Texas Comptroller as a retailer or wholesaler actively engaged in the business of selling tangible personal property.
rules.summary: Only registered_retailer or registered_wholesaler registration types are eligible to claim the resale exemption.

rules.description: Property purchased for resale must not be consumed or used by the buyer prior to or during resale. Property that is consumed in a service operation (e.g., food prepared and served on premises) does not qualify for resale exemption.
eligible_product_categories: tangible goods sold in original or substantially unaltered form
ineligible_product_categories: food consumed at point of service
rules.summary: Property consumed by the buyer during a service operation is not eligible for resale exemption; it must be resold in substantially unaltered form.

rules.description: A valid Texas resale certificate must contain all required fields: buyer legal name, buyer Texas taxpayer identification number, seller name, description of property to be purchased, stated reason for exemption, authorized signature, and certificate date.
rules.summary: Certificate must include buyer name, taxpayer ID, seller name, property description, exemption reason, signature, and date.

rules.description: The resale exemption does not apply to services. Contracts for services, professional fees, and labor charges are not exempt under the resale certificate even when provided by a registered retailer.
rules.summary: Services are not tangible personal property and do not qualify for the resale exemption regardless of the buyer's registration status.

rules.description: A Texas resale certificate is valid for four years from the date of issuance unless the seller has reason to believe the certificate is no longer valid. Expired certificates must be renewed before the exemption can continue to apply.
rules.summary: Resale certificates are valid for four years from issuance date; an expired certificate does not support a current exemption claim.

rules.description: Raw materials and components that are incorporated into or become part of tangible personal property manufactured for sale are exempt from Texas sales and use tax.
ineligible_product_categories: equipment used only indirectly in production
rules.summary: Raw materials and component parts physically incorporated into manufactured goods for sale are exempt; buyer must be a manufacturer.

rules.description: Machinery and equipment used directly and exclusively in the manufacturing process are exempt. The equipment must be integral to the production process, not merely helpful or supportive.
rules.summary: Equipment used directly in manufacturing is exempt; equipment used only for support, shipping, or administration is not.

rules.description: To qualify for the manufacturing exemption, the buyer must be engaged in the manufacture of tangible personal property for sale. Service businesses, even those that produce incidental physical outputs, are not manufacturers under Texas law.
rules.summary: Only entities registered as manufacturers and engaged in production of tangible goods for sale qualify; service providers are ineligible.

rules.description: Office supplies, furniture, and administrative equipment are explicitly excluded from the manufacturing exemption even when purchased by a qualified manufacturer. These items must be taxed at full rate.
rules.summary: Office supplies and administrative equipment are not exempt even for qualified manufacturers; the exemption is limited to production-related purchases.

rules.description: Items purchased primarily for use in a service business do not qualify for the manufacturing exemption even if some incidental manufacturing activity occurs.
ineligible_product_categories: tools used primarily in service operations
rules.summary: Service businesses are not eligible for the manufacturing exemption; items used in service delivery remain taxable.

rules.description: A valid Texas manufacturing exemption certificate must contain all required fields: buyer legal name, Texas taxpayer identification number, seller name, description of property or equipment, exemption reason stating manufacturing use, authorized signature, and date.
rules.summary: Manufacturing exemption certificates must include all required fields including signature; missing any required field invalidates the certificate.

rules.description: Component parts that become a physical component of the finished manufactured product and lose their separate identity are exempt. This includes consumable materials used up in the manufacturing process.
eligible_product_categories: component parts becoming part of finished product
rules.summary: Materials and parts that are physically incorporated into or consumed during production of the final product qualify for the exemption.

rules.description: Equipment must be used in the actual manufacturing or processing operation to qualify. Equipment used only before the manufacturing process begins or after it ends (e.g., storage, shipping, retail display) does not qualify.
eligible_product_categories: quality control equipment integral to production
rules.summary: Equipment must be integral to the actual production process; pre-production and post-production equipment does not qualify.

rules.description: Farm machinery, equipment, and supplies used exclusively in the production of agricultural products for sale are exempt from Texas sales and use tax.
rules.summary: Agricultural producers may purchase farm machinery, equipment, seeds, feed, and supplies used in agricultural production exempt from sales tax.

rules.description: To claim the agricultural exemption, the buyer must be engaged in the business of producing agricultural products for sale, including crops, livestock, poultry, or timber. The buyer must hold a valid Texas agricultural and timber registration number.
rules.summary: Only entities engaged in commercial agricultural production and registered as agricultural_producer are eligible; retailers, wholesalers, and manufacturers are not.

rules.description: Eligible categories under the agricultural exemption include: tractors, combines, and farm machinery; irrigation equipment; livestock feed; fertilizer and agricultural chemicals; seeds and plants; and veterinary supplies used in livestock production.
rules.summary: The exemption covers farm machinery, irrigation, feed, fertilizer, seeds, and veterinary supplies used in commercial agricultural production.

rules.description: Items purchased for personal use, residential use, or recreational purposes do not qualify for the agricultural exemption even when purchased by a registered agricultural producer.
ineligible_product_categories: personal vehicles not used in farming
rules.summary: Personal or residential use items are excluded from the agricultural exemption even when purchased by a qualified agricultural producer.

rules.description: A valid Texas agricultural exemption certificate must contain all required fields: buyer legal name, Texas agricultural and timber registration number, seller name, description of items to be purchased, stated agricultural use, authorized signature, and date.
rules.summary: Agricultural exemption certificates must include all required fields; any missing required field invalidates the certificate.

rules.description: Equipment and machinery used directly in agricultural production operations are exempt. This includes equipment for land preparation, planting, cultivation, harvesting, and transportation of agricultural products from the farm.
rules.summary: Equipment directly used in land prep, planting, cultivation, and harvesting qualifies; post-farm distribution equipment does not.
